Campaigns: npnjs.com phishing backdoored npm packages

Synopsis

StepSecurity confirmed @pkgjs/core 0.2.8 as one of the npm packages affected by the July 2025 npnjs.com maintainer phishing campaign.

Story

@pkgjs/core was another legitimate package caught in the npnjs.com phishing campaign. The attacker used stolen npm publishing access, so the malicious release appeared under the real package coordinate.

Version 0.2.8 was the affected release. The compromise followed the same pattern as the Prettier tooling packages: a registry publish with no ordinary source-review path behind it.

The package's role in the ecosystem made install-time execution dangerous even without a large user-facing application. Developer machines and CI runners often install tooling packages in environments with credentials and network reach.

This record stays concise because the public reporting names the package and version but gives less package-specific payload detail. The campaign record carries the shared phishing infrastructure and payload behavior.
